title: Scenario-driven quarterly roadmap: three-path cadence for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines a scenario-driven approach for the quarterly roadmap that explicitly ties Hosted API feature work and Model Catalog ops to three plausible business/hardware scenarios: 1) Aggressive Growth (rapid usage and new enterprise wins), 2) Steady Optimization (moderate growth; prioritize cost/latency), and 3) Stability-first (conservative; prioritize SLAs and security). Each path includes: prioritized initiatives, resource assumptions, gating criteria, and rollback/playbook instructions. The goal is to make Q1 commitments resilient to changes in demand or infra availability while linking every initiative to at least one measurable OKR (latency, cost per token, and model quality regression). Deliverables: a) prioritized model lineup for Hosted API with migration and retirement windows, b) canary and A/B rollout templates for model swaps, c) cross-functional dependency map (infra, runtime, console, security), and d) evaluation harness to catch regressions before canary release. We will use this ticket as the canonical artifact for the quarter-level decision points and as the source of truth for the roadmap commit that we present to Exec and Sales Engineering.

acceptance_criteria: OKR tiebacks for each prioritized initiative documented and owner-assigned

Dependency map reviewed and mitigations for top 3 risks agreed
Playbook for model rollback and fallback routing uploaded to Confluence
Stakeholder signoff (Product, Infra, SRE, Research) captured in comments
metrics: P95 latency for top-3 hosted models <= 200ms in steady path
Token cost per 1k tokens reduced >= 12% against baseline in steady/aggressive paths
Model-quality regression < 1% measured on core eval set for any model swap
Canary error rate < 0.5% during canary windows or automatic rollback
